captions.detailed: This 3D model is a solid cylindrical wire twisting jig. It features three shallow, semi-circular guide channels carved into the top outer edge, spaced evenly at 120-degree intervals. The cylindrical body is tall and smooth, with a flat top and bottom surface, designed to guide multiple wire strands as they are twisted together.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric wire-twisting jig in OpenSCAD. The design should consist of a main cylinder of adjustable radius and height, with a customizable number of wire channels carved into its outer perimeter at calculated angles, and an optional central wire channel.
captions.factory: The script uses a difference() operation to subtract wire channels from a main cylinder primitive of size jigRad and jigHeight. Inside a for-loop running from 1 to numStrand, it calculates the angular rotation and translational offset of the wire channels based on the wireRad, jigRad, and numStrand. These channels are generated as elongated cylinders, rotated using rotate() with calculated trigonometric angles (atan, sin, cos) and subtracted from the main body. An optional central cylinder is also conditionally subtracted if the center variable is enabled.
